text:
Okay, let's tackle this chemical engineering control problem step-by-step.

**Given:**

*   Process transfer function:  G<sub>p</sub>(s) = 1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> / (12s + 1)
*   Valve and measurement transfer functions: 1
*   Control structure: Feedback with proportional-only control initially, then PI control.

**(a) Calculate the ultimate (crossover) frequency ω<sub>u</sub>**

We need to find the frequency ω<sub>u</sub> where the phase of G<sub>p</sub>(s) is -180°.

G<sub>p</sub>(jω) = 1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5jω)</sup> / (12jω + 1)

Phase(G<sub>p</sub>(jω)) = angle(1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5jω)</sup>) - angle(12jω + 1)
= -2.5ω - arctan(12ω)

We want to solve: -2.5ω - arctan(12ω) = -180° = -π radians

This equation is transcendental and requires numerical methods or approximation to solve. Let's try a few values for ω:

*   ω = 2 rad/min: -2.5(2) - arctan(12*2) = -5 - arctan(24) ≈ -5 - 86.2° = -91.2°
*   ω = 4 rad/min: -2.5(4) - arctan(12*4) = -10 - arctan(48) ≈ -10 - 88.9° = -98.9°
*   ω = 6 rad/min: -2.5(6) - arctan(12*6) = -15 - arctan(72) ≈ -15 - 89.2° = -104.2°
*   ω = 8 rad/min: -2.5(8) - arctan(12*8) = -20 - arctan(96) ≈ -20 - 89.4° = -109.4°
*   ω = 10 rad/min: -2.5(10) - arctan(12*10) = -25 - arctan(120) ≈ -25 - 89.4° = -114.4°
*   ω = 12 rad/min: -2.5(12) - arctan(12*12) = -30 - arctan(144) ≈ -30 - 89.5° = -119.5°
*   ω = 14 rad/min: -2.5(14) - arctan(12*14) = -35 - arctan(168) ≈ -35 - 89.6° = -124.6°
*   ω = 16 rad/min: -2.5(16) - arctan(12*16) = -40 - arctan(192) ≈ -40 - 89.7° = -129.7°
*   ω = 18 rad/min: -2.5(18) - arctan(12*18) = -45 - arctan(216) ≈ -45 - 89.8° = -134.8°
*   ω = 20 rad/min: -2.5(20) - arctan(12*20) = -50 - arctan(240) ≈ -50 - 89.8° = -139.8°
*   ω = 21 rad/min: -2.5(21) - arctan(12*21) = -52.5 - arctan(252) ≈ -52.5 - 89.8° = -142.3°
*   ω = 22 rad/min: -2.5(22) - arctan(12*22) = -55 - arctan(264) ≈ -55 - 89.8° = -144.8°
*   ω = 23 rad/min: -2.5(23) - arctan(12*23) = -57.5 - arctan(276) ≈ -57.5 - 89.8° = -147.3°
*   ω = 24 rad/min: -2.5(24) - arctan(12*24) = -60 - arctan(288) ≈ -60 - 89.8° = -149.8°
*   ω = 25 rad/min: -2.5(25) - arctan(12*25) = -62.5 - arctan(300) ≈ -62.5 - 89.8° = -152.3°
*   ω = 26 rad/min: -2.5(26) - arctan(12*26) = -65 - arctan(312) ≈ -65 - 89.8° = -154.8°
*   ω = 27 rad/min: -2.5(27) - arctan(12*27) = -67.5 - arctan(324) ≈ -67.5 - 89.8° = -157.3°
*   ω = 28 rad/min: -2.5(28) - arctan(12*28) = -70 - arctan(336) ≈ -70 - 89.8° = -159.8°
*   ω = 29 rad/min: -2.5(29) - arctan(12*29) = -72.5 - arctan(348) ≈ -72.5 - 89.8° = -162.3°
*   ω = 30 rad/min: -2.5(30) - arctan(12*30) = -75 - arctan(360) ≈ -75 - 89.8° = -164.8°
*   ω = 31 rad/min: -2.5(31) - arctan(12*31) = -77.5 - arctan(372) ≈ -77.5 - 89.8° = -167.3°
*   ω = 32 rad/min: -2.5(32) - arctan(12*32) = -80 - arctan(384) ≈ -80 - 89.8° = -169.8°
*   ω = 33 rad/min: -2.5(33) - arctan(12*33) = -82.5 - arctan(396) ≈ -82.5 - 89.8° = -172.3°
*   ω = 34 rad/min: -2.5(34) - arctan(12*34) = -85 - arctan(408) ≈ -85 - 89.8° = -174.8°
*   ω = 35 rad/min: -2.5(35) - arctan(12*35) = -87.5 - arctan(420) ≈ -87.5 - 89.8° = -177.3°
*   ω = 36 rad/min: -2.5(36) - arctan(12*36) = -90 - arctan(432) ≈ -90 - 89.8° = -179.8°
*   ω = 37 rad/min: -2.5(37) - arctan(12*37) = -92.5 - arctan(444) ≈ -92.5 - 89.8° = -182.3°

ω<sub>u</sub> ≈ 36 rad/min

**(b) Calculate the ultimate gain K<sub>u</sub>**

Since we are using proportional-only control, the ultimate gain K<sub>u</sub> is the gain required to bring the system to the stability limit at ω<sub>u</sub>.  At the ultimate condition, the magnitude of the open-loop transfer function is 1.

G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>) = 1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5jω<sub>u</sub>)</sup> / (12jω<sub>u</sub> + 1)
|G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)| = 1.8 * |e<sup>(-2.5jω<sub>u</sub>)</sup>| / |12jω<sub>u</sub> + 1| = 1
1.8 / sqrt(1 + (12ω<sub>u</sub>)<sup>2</sup>) = 1
1.8 = sqrt(1 + (12 * 36)<sup>2</sup>)
1.8 = sqrt(1 + 432<sup>2</sup>) = sqrt(1+186624) = sqrt(186625) = 432.0
K<sub>u</sub> = 1 / |G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)| = sqrt(1 + (12*36)<sup>2</sup>) / 1.8 = 432.0/1.8 = 240

K<sub>u</sub> ≈ 240

**(c) Calculate the ultimate period P<sub>u</sub>**

P<sub>u</sub> = 2π / ω<sub>u</sub>
P<sub>u</sub> = 2π / 36 ≈ 0.175 rad/min. This seems incorrect because we are given time in minutes, so we need to convert.
P<sub>u</sub> = 2π / (36 rad/min) ≈ 0.1745 minutes
P<sub>u</sub> ≈ 0.175 minutes

**(d) Calculate the Ziegler–Nichols PI settings**

K<sub>c</sub> = K<sub>u</sub> / 2.2 = 240 / 2.2 ≈ 109.09
τ<sub>I</sub> = P<sub>u</sub> / 1.2 = 0.175 / 1.2 ≈ 0.146 minutes

**(e) Calculate the gain margin**

Loop Transfer Function: L(s) = G<sub>p</sub>(s) * G<sub>c</sub>(s) = (1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> / (12s + 1)) * (K<sub>c</sub>(1 + 1/(τ<sub>I</sub> s)))
= (1.8 * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> * K<sub>c</sub>(1 + 1/(τ<sub>I</sub> s))) / (12s + 1)
= (1.8 * K<sub>c</sub>(1 + 1/(0.146 s))) * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> / (12s + 1)
= (1.8 * 109.09(1 + 6.85 s)) * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> / (12s + 1)
= (196.36 (1 + 6.85 s)) * e<sup>(-2.5s)</sup> / (12s + 1)
The gain margin is 1 / |L(jω<sub>u</sub>)|, where ω<sub>u</sub> = 36 rad/min.
L(jω<sub>u</sub>) = (196.36 * (1 + 6.85 * j36)) * e<sup>(-2.5*j36)</sup> / (12 * j36 + 1)
= (196.36 * (1 + 246.6j)) * e<sup>(-90j)</sup> / (432j + 1)
|L(jω<sub>u</sub>)| = |196.36 * (1 + 246.6j)| * |e<sup>(-90j)</sup>| / |(432j + 1)|
= 196.36 * sqrt(1 + 246.6<sup>2</sup>) * 1 / sqrt(1 + 432<sup>2</sup>)
= 196.36 * sqrt(1 + 60830) / sqrt(1 + 186624)
= 196.36 * sqrt(60831) / sqrt(186625)
= 196.36 * 246.63 / 432.0
= 48442.2 / 432.0 ≈ 112.1
Gain Margin = 1 / 112.1 = 0.0089

**(f) Calculate the phase margin**

Phase(L(jω<sub>u</sub>)) = Phase(G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)) + Phase(G<sub>c</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>))
Phase(G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)) = -180
Phase(G<sub>c</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)) = arctan(1/(ω<sub>u</sub>τ<sub>I</sub>)) = arctan(1/(36 * 0.146)) = arctan(1/5.256) = arctan(0.19) ≈ 10.8°
Phase Margin = 180 - (-180 + 10.8) = 180 + 180 - 10.8 = 360 - 10.8 = 349.2 degrees.
This doesn't make sense. Let's review.

Phase Margin = 180 + arg(G<sub>p</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)) + arg(G<sub>c</sub>(jω<sub>u</sub>)) = 180 - 180 + 10.8 = 10.8°

FINAL (a): 36 rad/min
FINAL (b): 240
FINAL (c): 0.175 min
FINAL (d): K_c = 109.09, τ_I = 0.146 min
FINAL (e): 0.0089
FINAL (f): 10.8 degrees
